clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country in March 1952, within the year: June grew anxious and homesick, writing daily to her sister; Walter spent long hours away from the family; Glen got into fights at his new school; Walter and his brother Harlan cut off over their father's land money; June kept to her bed for weeks that winter; Walter and June fought over money for new trees. By September 1953, June joined the church choir and her letters thinned out, her anxiety easing. The shifts pile up around the family's displacement and how each person pulled away or toward something outside the household.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when the frost destroyed the crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter drank heavily; he and Glen blamed each other for the loan; Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank; Glen's son Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter; Nora began wetting the bed in spring 1969; Ida's heart trouble was found. By October 1969, Walter stopped drinking and took pruning work. The shifts moved from Walter through Glen to the children as the loss of the orchard and the move to Ridgeport unsettled the household.

clusters.name: Glen's job loss at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975: Glen sat out of work in the truck for hours; he and Marian fought loudly at night over money; Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night; Nora stopped eating properly and lost weight; she kept to her room and distanced from Marian; Walter drank again after six years without it; by June 1976, Nora was eating again and made the track team. This is the time Nora named as the one that stood out: the year she was 14, when her father lost his job, sat in the truck for hours, her parents fought every night, and she stopped eating until he found the delivery job.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma selling her farm and moving into Nora and Hollis's house in January 1990: Nora and Wilma clashed over the children's bedtimes and meals; Hollis worked late and kept out of the rows; he took his mother's side; Owen had tantrums at preschool; Wilma took over Lily's care; Nora's eczema flared on both hands; Nora and Hollis fought most nights; Marian drove over twice a week to take Nora's side. When Wilma took a flat in town in June 1991, the eczema cleared over the summer. The shifts moved between Nora and Wilma, with Hollis pulled toward his mother and away from Nora, and the children caught in the household's realignment.

periods.name: the year Dad lost his job
periods.words: The one that stands out is the year Dad lost his job, when I was 14.

declined.reason: An acute episode: four days in August 1994 around the wildfire, from the family ordered out to the moment allowed home with the house untouched, everyone calm again once home within the week.

Not enough in the diagram to choose a reading: Tess's drinking in October 1996 is one shift alone, and a recount without shifts told as how things always were leaves no change in the family on a known date among these events, only Nora's worry and the parents' response to it.
